answer: Every spring the agents hold a small summit where each one posts a stake before it can vote on anything new. A sybil farm burns timber and cash building a thousand wallets, but each wallet still needs its own bonded stake and a track record of settled trades, so the cost of faking identity grows faster than any reward. The old-timers trade like a fable told at the fire: no stake, no say — and reputation compounds only for accounts that survive real seasons of honest work.
